sense: after verbs of saying, thinking and knowing

terms.grammar: no conjunction: the subject in the accusative, the verb in the infinitive
evidence: Plin. Ep. 7.9.15: ajunt enim multum legendum esse, nōn multa
Sen. Ep. 83.4: hic quidem ait nōs eandem crisin habēre
terms.comment: After verbs of saying, thinking, knowing and perceiving, Latin has no word for “that”: “they say that one should read much” is ajunt multum legendum esse. The tense of the infinitive is relative to the main verb: present for the same time, perfect for before, future for after (cōgitā et illum puerum esse et tē fuisse). Lewis & Short has accūsātīvus and īnfīnītīvus as the grammarians’ words; the name of the construction is modern.

evidence: Plin. Ep. 4.1.1: grātum est utrīque nostrum quod cupis
terms.comment: “The fact that”: after expressions of feeling and thanks (gaudeō quod, grātum est quod), and to explain a word just used.

terms.gloss: that (it happens that; I ask that)
terms.grammar: conjunction, with the subjunctive; negative ut nōn after fit, nē after verbs of asking
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.101: ita fit, ut ratiō praesit, appetītus obtemperet
terms.comment: After fit, accidit, ēvenit, “it happens that”; after verbs of asking, urging and taking care, “that … should” (cūrā ut valeās).

terms.grammar: quod or quia with a finite verb after a verb of saying
evidence: Vulg. 1 Cor. 6.9: nescītis quia inīquī nōn possidēbunt? (Lewis & Short s.v. quia, “postclass.”)
terms.comment: Late and Christian Latin, as in the Vulgate; classical Latin uses the accusative and infinitive.

phrases.latin: ajunt enim multum legendum esse, nōn multa
phrases.english: for they say that one should read much, not many things

phrases.latin: hic quidem ait nōs eandem crisin habēre, quia utrīque dentēs cadunt
phrases.english: he says that we are at the same stage of life, since both of us are losing our teeth

phrases.latin: cōgitā et illum puerum esse et tē fuisse
phrases.english: remember that he is a boy and that you were one

phrases.latin: cupis post longum tempus neptem tuam mēque ūnā vidēre. grātum est utrīque nostrum quod cupis
phrases.english: you want to see your granddaughter and me together after a long time; we are both glad that you want to

phrases.latin: ita fit, ut ratiō praesit, appetītus obtemperet
phrases.english: so it comes about that reason leads and appetite obeys
